topic: Data Preprocessing: Handling Outliers, Missing Values, and Skewed Data

questions.scenario: A financial fraud detection engine processes credit card transaction records where the 'transaction_amount' feature is severely right-skewed with extreme positive outliers, and contains genuine non-fraudulent authorization checks recorded as exactly zero dollars. The downstream machine learning model is an L2-regularized Logistic Regression classifier that requires continuous features to exhibit stabilized variance and approximate normality. Applying standard Box-Cox transformation throws an arithmetic runtime error, while manual log transformations like log(x + c) introduce arbitrary sensitivity to the choice of constant c.
questions.question: Which power transformation method mathematically supports non-positive values directly and optimizes the power parameter via Maximum Likelihood Estimation without introducing an arbitrary shift constant?
options: B) Box-Cox Transformation with Laplace smoothing
questions.explanation: The Yeo-Johnson transformation extends the Box-Cox family by allowing zero and negative values. While Box-Cox is strictly defined for strictly positive values (x > 0), Yeo-Johnson provides piecewise continuous equations for x >= 0 and x < 0 parametrized by lambda, where lambda is determined by Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE). This avoids heuristic constants (e.g., log(x + 1)), which distort the variance structure at lower thresholds.

questions.scenario: A smart intensive-care unit (ICU) system collects continuous 128-channel vital telemetry at 50 Hz. Due to intermittent sensor disconnects and RF noise, roughly 6% of the telemetry vectors suffer from Missing Completely at Random (MCAR) values. An offline batch model uses IterativeImputer (MICE with Bayesian Ridge), but deploying this in production violates the strict edge-device inference latency budget (p99 latency must remain under 15 milliseconds). Conversely, univariate mean/median imputation causes severe downstream classification drift by destroying inter-channel cross-covariance.
questions.question: Which imputation strategy best balances the preservation of cross-channel covariance with strict real-time edge latency (sub-15ms) constraints?
options: A) K-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) imputation with a full spatial brute-force scan per frame
B) Pre-trained Denoising Autoencoder or Incremental Low-Rank Matrix Factorization projection
C) Complete Case Analysis (Listwise Deletion) per time slice
D) MissForest (Random Forest-based imputation) initialized with cold-start zero imputation
questions.correct_answer_text: B) Pre-trained Denoising Autoencoder or Incremental Low-Rank Matrix Factorization projection
questions.explanation: Pre-trained Denoising Autoencoders (DAEs) or Low-Rank Matrix Projections (like Incremental SVD) compute imputations via forward-pass matrix multiplication (O(d * k) complexity), easily running in single-digit milliseconds on edge hardware while capturing complex inter-channel correlations. In contrast, MICE and MissForest require iterative convergence cycles that fail strict real-time SLAs, k-NN requires heavy pairwise search across reference buffers (O(N * d)), and Listwise Deletion discards valid temporal context critical in ICU telemetry.

questions.scenario: A semiconductor manufacturing facility monitors wafer quality using 300 highly collinear and multi-modal continuous sensor channels. Defective wafers represent less than 0.1% of samples. An engineer tries applying standard Minimum Covariance Determinant (MCD) to detect outliers via Mahalanobis distance, but it fails with a singular covariance matrix error. Next, the engineer applies standard Isolation Forest, but domain experts observe significant false alarms ('ghost anomalies') caused by unnatural axis-parallel bounding cuts slicing through tilted, highly-correlated multi-sensor manifolds.
questions.question: Which algorithm modification directly rectifies the axis-parallel hyper-rectangle partitioning artifact of standard Isolation Forests in high-dimensional correlated spaces without requiring full covariance matrix inversion?
options: A) Extended Isolation Forest (EIF) with random linear-combination hyperplanes
B) Local Outlier Factor (LOF) configured with Minkowski p=0.5 metric
C) Z-score standardization followed by feature-wise clipping at 3 standard deviations
D) Principal Component Imputation followed by univariate Grubbs' tests
questions.correct_answer_text: A) Extended Isolation Forest (EIF) with random linear-combination hyperplanes
questions.explanation: Standard Isolation Forest chooses split points uniformly along individual coordinate axes (axis-parallel orthogonal cuts), which causes structural bias and produces 'ghost anomalies' where no data points actually reside along oblique distributions. Extended Isolation Forest (EIF) resolves this by selecting random hyperplanes with arbitrary slope/orientation vectors (linear combinations of features) at each node. This naturally conforms to correlated manifolds and eliminates axis-aligned artifacts while retaining the O(n log n) scaling efficiency, avoiding covariance matrix inversion required by Mahalanobis/MCD.
